spec.hypothesis: Logistic regression with median imputation, standard scaling, and one-hot encoding already achieves 0.807 macro F1; adding a small ensemble (logistic + catboost) with class_weight balancing and ordinal/one-hot handling of the categorical column should improve robustness on this small, slightly imbalanced dataset.

Logistic regression with median imputation, standard scaling, and one-hot encoding already achieves 0.807 macro F1; adding a small ensemble (logistic + catboost) with class_weight balancing and ordinal/one-hot handling of the categorical column should improve robustness on this small, slightly imbalanced dataset.

The previous CatBoost failure likely stems from class_weight='balanced' combined with auto_class_weights='Balanced', which can cause parameter conflicts or invalid labels for CatBoost's balanced weighting. Removing class_weight from CatBoost (and using explicit class_weights instead) or dropping the ensemble in favor of a robust logistic regression plus a safer CatBoost configuration should fix the issue while maintaining strong macro F1.

The CatBoost failure under VotingClassifier is likely because class labels must be non-negative contiguous integers; combined with the imbalanced small dataset, a robust alternative is a soft-voting ensemble of a balanced logistic regression and a balanced RandomForest, both wrapped so that the whole preprocessing (median/most-frequent imputation, scaling, one-hot with handle_unknown) is fitted inside the pipeline. RandomForest is stable, handles missing categories via the fitted OneHotEncoder, and gives strong macro-F1 on small tabular data without CatBoost-specific label constraints.
